sanskrit: tato vijñātacāritraḥ satkṛtya sa vimokṣitaḥ pariṣvaktaś ca sasnehaṃ mṛgendreṇa punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then, his character recognized, he was honoured, set free, and embraced again and again with affection by the lord of beasts.

sanskrit: anujñāpya mṛgendraṃ tu gomāyur nītiśāstravit tenāmarṣeṇa saṃtaptaḥ prāyam āsitum aicchata
english: But the jackal, learned in the science of polity, having taken leave of the lord of beasts and burning still with that resentment, wished to fast unto death.

sanskrit: śārdūlas tatra gomāyuṃ snehāt prasrutalocanaḥ avārayat sa dharmiṣṭhaṃ pūjayā pratipūjayan
english: There the tiger, his eyes brimming with tears of affection, held the jackal back, that most righteous one, honouring him in return with marks of honour.

sanskrit: taṃ sa gomāyur ālokya snehād āgatasaṃbhramam babhāṣe praṇato vākyaṃ bāṣpagadgadayā girā
english: Beholding him thus moved by affection into agitation, the jackal, bowing low, spoke these words in a voice choked with tears.

sanskrit: pūjito 'haṃ tvayā pūrvaṃ paścāc caiva vimānitaḥ pareṣām āspadaṃ nīto vastuṃ nārhāmy ahaṃ tvayi
english: "First I was honoured by you, and afterwards dishonoured; I was made the resort of others' designs. I am not fit to dwell with you any longer."

sanskrit: svasaṃtuṣṭāś cyutāḥ sthānān mānāt pratyavaropitāḥ svayaṃ copahṛtā bhṛtyā ye cāpy upahṛtāḥ paraiḥ
english: "Servants who were content, then fallen from their station, cast down from their honour, those withdrawn of their own accord, and those drawn away by enemies—

sanskrit: parikṣīṇāś ca lubdhāś ca krūrāḥ kārābhitāpitāḥ hṛtasvā mānino ye ca tyaktopāttā mahepsavaḥ
english: the impoverished, the greedy, the cruel, those tormented by imprisonment, the proud whose wealth has been seized, and those grasping ones who, once cast off, have been taken back—

sanskrit: saṃtāpitāś ca ye ke cid vyasanaughapratīkṣiṇaḥ antarhitāḥ sopahitāḥ sarve te parasādhanāḥ
english: and whoever have been afflicted, those lying in wait for a flood of calamities, those who lie concealed with hostile intent—all these become instruments of the foe."

sanskrit: avamānena yuktasya sthāpitasya ca me punaḥ kathaṃ yāsyasi viśvāsam aham eṣyāmi vā punaḥ
english: "Toward me, who was treated with contempt and then reinstated, how will you ever come to trust again, and how shall I again come to trust you?"

sanskrit: samartha iti saṃgṛhya sthāpayitvā parīkṣya ca kṛtaṃ ca samayaṃ bhittvā tvayāham avamānitaḥ
english: "Having taken me in as capable, having installed and tested me, you broke the agreement that was made and dishonoured me."

sanskrit: prathamaṃ yaḥ samākhyātaḥ śīlavān iti saṃsadi na vācyaṃ tasya vaiguṇyaṃ pratijñāṃ parirakṣatā
english: "Of one who has first been proclaimed a man of good character in the assembly, his fault should not be spoken of by one who would keep his pledge."

sanskrit: evaṃ cāvamatasyeha viśvāsaṃ kiṃ prayāsyasi tvayi caiva hy aviśvāse mamodvego bhaviṣyati
english: "How then will you place trust in one so slighted, and so long as I distrust you, my own disquiet will remain?"

sanskrit: śaṅkitas tvam ahaṃ bhītaḥ pare chidrānudarśinaḥ asnigdhāś caiva dustoṣāḥ karma caitad bahucchalam
english: "You are suspicious, I am afraid; the others are forever watching for an opening, unaffectionate and hard to satisfy—and this business is full of treachery."

sanskrit: duḥkhena śleṣyate bhinnaṃ śliṣṭaṃ duḥkhena bhidyate bhinnaśliṣṭā tu yā prītir na sā snehena vartate
english: "What is broken is rejoined only with difficulty, and what is joined is sundered only with difficulty; but a friendship that is severed and then patched together does not abide in true affection."

sanskrit: kaś cid eva hi bhītas tu dṛśyate na parātmanoḥ kāryāpekṣā hi vartante bhāvāḥ snigdhās tu durlabhāḥ
english: "It is but rarely that one is seen unafraid in dealings between oneself and another; the feelings men show are governed by self-interest, while genuine affection is hard to find."

sanskrit: suduḥkhaṃ puruṣajñānaṃ cittaṃ hy eṣāṃ calācalam samartho vāpy aśakto vā śateṣv eko 'dhigamyate
english: "The knowledge of men is most hard to attain, for their minds are unsteady and wavering; whether able or unable, scarcely one in a hundred is rightly understood."

sanskrit: akasmāt prakriyā nṝṇām akasmāc cāpakarṣaṇam śubhāśubhe mahattvaṃ ca prakartuṃ buddhilāghavāt
english: "Men's advancement comes without cause, and their casting down comes without cause; and out of fickleness of mind they are prone to make much of both good and ill."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ sāntvam uktvā dharmārthahetumat prasādayitvā rājānaṃ gomāyur vanam abhyagāt
english: Having spoken conciliation of many kinds, grounded in dharma and statecraft, and having appeased the king, the jackal went away into the forest.

sanskrit: agṛhyānunayaṃ tasya mṛgendrasya sa buddhimān gomāyuḥ prāyam āsīnas tyaktvā dehaṃ divaṃ yayau
english: Not accepting the entreaty of that lord of beasts, the wise jackal, having fasted unto death and abandoned his body, went to heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kiṃ pārthivena kartavyaṃ kiṃ ca kṛtvā sukhī bhavet tan mamācakṣva tattvena sarvaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: What ought a king to do, and by doing what does he become happy? Declare all this to me truly, O best of the upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu kāryaikaniścayam yathā rājñeha kartavyaṃ yac ca kṛtvā sukhī bhavet
english: Bhīṣma said: Come, I shall declare it to you; listen to the one sure rule of action—how a king ought to act here, and by doing what he becomes happy.

sanskrit: na tv evaṃ vartitavyaṃ sma yathedam anuśuśrumaḥ uṣṭrasya sumahad vṛttaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: One must not conduct oneself in the manner of which we have heard tell. There is a notable story of a camel; mark it, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: jātismaro mahān uṣṭraḥ prājāpatyayugodbhavaḥ tapaḥ sumahad ātiṣṭhad araṇye saṃśitavrataḥ
english: A great camel, who remembered his former births and was born in the age of Prajāpati, undertook a most severe austerity in the forest, firm in his vow.

sanskrit: tapasas tasya cānte vai prītimān abhavat prabhuḥ vareṇa chandayām āsa tataś cainaṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: At the close of that austerity the Lord became gratified, and the Grandfather then offered him the choice of a boon.

sanskrit: uṣṭra uvāca bhagavaṃs tvatprasādān me dīrghā grīvā bhaved iyam yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ yā gacchec carituṃ vibho
english: The camel said: O blessed one, by your grace may this neck of mine grow long, so that it may reach a full hundred yojanas to forage, O mighty lord.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam astv iti coktaḥ sa varadena mahātmanā pratilabhya varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yayāv uṣṭraḥ svakaṃ vanam
english: Bhīṣma said: "So be it," said the great-souled bestower of boons; and the camel, having obtained that excellent boon, went off to his own forest.

sanskrit: sa cakāra tad ālasyaṃ varadānāt sa durmatiḥ na caicchac carituṃ gantuṃ durātmā kālamohitaḥ
english: On account of that gift of a boon, the dull-witted creature gave himself over to sloth; deluded by fate and ill-natured, he no longer cared to walk about to forage.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit prasāryaivaṃ tāṃ grīvāṃ śatayojanām cacārāśrāntahṛdayo vātaś cāgāt tato mahān
english: Once, stretching out in this way his neck of a hundred yojanas, he grazed with an untiring heart; and thereupon a great wind arose.

sanskrit: sa guhāyāṃ śirogrīvaṃ nidhāya paśur ātmanaḥ āstātha varṣam abhyāgāt sumahat plāvayaj jagat
english: That beast, having laid his own head and neck within a cave, settled down; then a very great rain came on, flooding the world.

sanskrit: atha śītaparītāṅgo jambukaḥ kṣucchramānvitaḥ sadāras tāṃ guhām āśu praviveśa jalārditaḥ
english: Then a jackal, his limbs gripped by cold and worn with hunger, together with his mate, tormented by the water, quickly entered that cave.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā māṃsajīvī tu subhṛśaṃ kṣucchramānvitaḥ abhakṣayat tato grīvām uṣṭrasya bharatarṣabha
english: And that flesh-eater, beholding it and sorely wasted with hunger, thereupon devoured the neck of the camel, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yadā tv abudhyatātmānaṃ bhakṣyamāṇaṃ sa vai paśuḥ tadā saṃkocane yatnam akarod bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ
english: But when that beast became aware that he himself was being eaten, then, grievously pained, he made an effort to draw his neck back in.

sanskrit: yāvad ūrdhvam adhaś caiva grīvāṃ saṃkṣipate paśuḥ tāvat tena sadāreṇa jambukena sa bhakṣitaḥ
english: As the beast contracted his neck this way and that, up and down, even so was he devoured by that jackal and its mate.

sanskrit: sa hatvā bhakṣayitvā ca jambukoṣṭraṃ tatas tadā vigate vātavarṣe ca niścakrāma guhāmukhāt
english: And the jackal, having slain the camel and eaten of it, then, when the wind and rain had passed, came forth from the mouth of the cave.

sanskrit: evaṃ durbuddhinā prāptam uṣṭreṇa nidhanaṃ tadā ālasyasya kramāt paśya mahad doṣam upāgatam
english: Thus was destruction met with by that ill-witted camel; behold the great calamity that came upon him through the course of his sloth.

sanskrit: tvam apy etaṃ vidhiṃ tyaktvā yogena niyatendriyaḥ vartasva buddhimūlaṃ hi vijayaṃ manur abravīt
english: You too, abandoning this manner of conduct, with senses restrained through discipline, should act; for Manu declared that victory is rooted in intelligence.

sanskrit: buddhiśreṣṭhāni karmāṇi bāhumadhyāni bhārata tāni jaṅghājaghanyāni bhārapratyavarāṇi ca
english: Deeds of intellect are the best, O Bhārata; those of the arms are middling; those of the legs are lowest, and mere bearing of burdens is lowest of all.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ tiṣṭhati dakṣasya saṃgṛhītendriyasya ca guptamantraśrutavataḥ susahāyasya cānagha
english: The kingdom abides with one who is capable, who has mastered his senses, who keeps his counsel secret, who is learned, and who has good helpers, O sinless one.

sanskrit: parīkṣyakāriṇo 'rthāś ca tiṣṭhantīha yudhiṣṭhira sahāyayuktena mahī kṛtsnā śakyā praśāsitum
english: And the affairs of one who acts after due examination prosper here, Yudhiṣṭhira; with good helpers the whole earth can be governed.

sanskrit: idaṃ hi sadbhiḥ kathitaṃ vidhijñaiḥ; purā mahendrapratimaprabhāva mayāpi coktaṃ tava śāstradṛṣṭyā; tvam atra yuktaḥ pracarasva rājan
english: This was told of old by the good who know the law, O you whose majesty equals great Indra's; and I too have spoken it to you according to the vision of the scriptures—so apply yourself diligently to it and go forth, O king.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rājā rājyam anuprāpya durbalo bharatarṣabha amitrasyātivṛddhasya kathaṃ tiṣṭhed asādhanaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a weak king, O bull of the Bhāratas, has obtained a kingdom, how should he hold his ground, without resources, against an enemy of overwhelming strength?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam saritāṃ caiva saṃvādaṃ sāgarasya ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale, a dialogue of the rivers and the ocean, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: surārinilayaḥ śaśvat sāgaraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ papraccha saritaḥ sarvāḥ saṃśayaṃ jātam ātmanaḥ
english: The ocean, the everlasting abode of the foes of the gods, lord of the rivers, asked all the rivers about a doubt that had arisen within him.

sanskrit: samūlaśākhān paśyāmi nihatāṃś chāyino drumān yuṣmābhir iha pūrṇābhir anyāṃs tatra na vetasam
english: "I see shade-giving trees struck down root and branch, carried here by you in your fullness—yet among them never the reed."

sanskrit: akāyaś cālpasāraś ca vetasaḥ kūlajaś ca vaḥ avajñāya naśakyo vā kiṃ cid vā tena vaḥ kṛtam
english: "The reed is slight of body and of little substance, and grows upon your very banks; is it that, despising it, you cannot uproot it, or has it rendered you some service?"

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi sarvāsām eva vo matam yathā kūlāni cemāni bhittvā nānīyate vaśam
english: "This I wish to hear—the opinion of you all—why it is that the reed is not brought under sway, while you break down these banks of yours."

sanskrit: tataḥ prāha nadī gaṅgā vākyam uttaram arthavat hetumad grāhakaṃ caiva sāgaraṃ saritāṃ patim
english: Then the river Gaṅgā spoke an answering word, meaningful, reasoned, and convincing, to the ocean, the lord of rivers.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhanty ete yathāsthānaṃ nagā hy ekaniketanāḥ tatas tyajanti tat sthānaṃ prātilomyād acetasaḥ
english: "These trees stand fixed each in its place, each rooted in a single spot; then, out of senseless contrariness, they forfeit that place."

sanskrit: vetaso vegam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā namati netaraḥ sa ca vege 'bhyatikrānte sthānam āsādya tiṣṭhati
english: "The reed, seeing the rushing current come on, bows down, but the other does not; and when the current has passed by, it regains its place and stands."

sanskrit: kālajñaḥ samayajñaś ca sadā vaśyaś ca nodrumaḥ anulomas tathāstabdhas tena nābhyeti vetasaḥ
english: "Knowing the time and knowing the occasion, ever yielding and not rising stubbornly, compliant and unstiffened—and for that reason the reed comes to no harm."

sanskrit: mārutodakavegena ye namanty unnamanti ca oṣadhyaḥ pādapā gulmā na te yānti parābhavam
english: "Those herbs, trees, and shrubs that bend down and rise again with the force of wind and water—they do not meet with overthrow."

sanskrit: yo hi śatror vivṛddhasya prabhor vadhavināśane pūrvaṃ na sahate vegaṃ kṣipram eva sa naśyati
english: "For he who, when a mighty foe has grown strong and bent on slaughter and destruction, does not at the first bear with his onset, swiftly perishes."

sanskrit: sārāsāraṃ balaṃ vīryam ātmano dviṣataś ca yaḥ jānan vicarati prājño na sa yāti parābhavam
english: "But the wise man who moves about knowing the strength and weakness, the power and the valour, both of himself and of his foe—he does not come to overthrow."

sanskrit: evam eva yadā vidvān manyetātibalaṃ ripum saṃśrayed vaitasīṃ vṛttim evaṃ prajñānalakṣaṇam
english: "Just so, when the wise man deems his enemy too strong, let him resort to the way of the reed; this is the mark of true discernment."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vidvān mūrkhapragalbhena mṛdus tīkṣṇena bhārata ākruśyamānaḥ sadasi kathaṃ kuryād ariṃdama
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a learned man, gentle, is reviled in the assembly by a fool grown insolent and harsh, what should he do, O Bhārata, O subduer of foes?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śrūyatāṃ pṛthivīpāla yathaiṣo 'rtho 'nugīyate sadā sucetāḥ sahate narasyehālpacetasaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear, O guardian of the earth, how this matter is sung. The man of good understanding ever bears with the abuse of the man of feeble understanding.

sanskrit: aruṣyan kruśyamānasya sukṛtaṃ nāma vindati duṣkṛtaṃ cātmano marṣī ruṣyaty evāpamārṣṭi vai
english: By not growing angry when reviled, the forbearing man gains the other's merit and is freed of his own ill deeds; while the one who answers anger with anger wipes away that gain.

sanskrit: ṭiṭṭibhaṃ tam upekṣeta vāśamānam ivāturam lokavidveṣam āpanno niṣphalaṃ pratipadyate
english: One should disregard such a man as one would a lapwing crying out as if in distress; for having incurred the world's hatred, he gains nothing for his pains.

sanskrit: iti sa ślāghate nityaṃ tena pāpena karmaṇā idam ukto mayā kaś cit saṃmato janasaṃsadi sa tatra vrīḍitaḥ śuṣko mṛtakalpo 'vatiṣṭhati
english: Thus he forever boasts of that base deed, saying, "Such a one, esteemed in the assembly of men, was told off by me!"—while the other stands there abashed, withered, and as good as dead.

sanskrit: ślāghann aślāghanīyena karmaṇā nirapatrapaḥ upekṣitavyo dāntena tādṛśaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ
english: One who boasts shamelessly of a deed not worth boasting of—such a basest of men is to be disregarded by him who is self-controlled.

sanskrit: yad yad brūyād alpamatis tat tad asya sahet sadā prākṛto hi praśaṃsan vā nindan vā kiṃ kariṣyati vane kāka ivābuddhir vāśamāno nirarthakam
english: Whatever the dull-minded man may say, one should ever bear with it; for what can a base fellow do, whether he praise or blame, croaking witlessly to no purpose like a crow in the forest?

sanskrit: yadi vāgbhiḥ prayogaḥ syāt prayoge pāpakarmaṇaḥ vāg evārtho bhavet tasya na hy evārtho jighāṃsataḥ
english: If the contest of the evildoer were waged only with words, then words alone would be his object; but no such limited object belongs to one who seeks to destroy.

sanskrit: niṣekaṃ viparītaṃ sa ācaṣṭe vṛttaceṣṭayā mayūra iva kaupīnaṃ nṛtyan saṃdarśayann iva
english: By his conduct and gestures he proclaims the baseness of his own begetting, like a peacock dancing and as it were displaying its nakedness.

sanskrit: yasyāvācyaṃ na loke 'sti nākāryaṃ vāpi kiṃ cana vācaṃ tena na saṃdadhyāc chuciḥ saṃkliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: With one for whom there is nothing in the world unspeakable and nothing whatever undoable, the pure man should hold no converse, for his deeds are foul.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ guṇavādī yaḥ parokṣaṃ tu vinindakaḥ sa mānavaḥ śvaval loke naṣṭalokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: The man who praises one's virtues to the face but slanders behind the back—such a man is like a dog in the world, bound for the loss of all blessed worlds.

sanskrit: tādṛg janaśatasyāpi yad dadāti juhoti ca parokṣeṇāpavādena tan nāśayati sa kṣaṇāt
english: Whatever such a man gives in charity or offers in sacrifice, even for a hundred men, he destroys it in an instant by his slander behind the back.

sanskrit: tasmāt prājño naraḥ sadyas tādṛśaṃ pāpacetasam varjayet sādhubhir varjyaṃ sārameyāmiṣaṃ yathā
english: Therefore the wise man should at once shun such a one of evil mind, as the good shun the flesh that a dog has touched.

sanskrit: parivādaṃ bruvāṇo hi durātmā vai mahātmane prakāśayati doṣān svān sarpaḥ phaṇam ivocchritam
english: For the wicked man, uttering reproach against the noble, lays bare his own faults, as a serpent raises high its lifted hood.

sanskrit: taṃ svakarmāṇi kurvāṇaṃ pratikartuṃ ya icchati bhasmakūṭa ivābuddhiḥ kharo rajasi majjati
english: He who, witless, wishes to retaliate against such a one as he carries on his own doings, sinks into the dust, like an ass plunging into a heap of ashes.

sanskrit: manuṣyaśālāvṛkam apraśāntaṃ; janāpavāde satataṃ niviṣṭam mātaṅgam unmattam ivonnadantaṃ; tyajeta taṃ śvānam ivātiraudram
english: That hyena in human shape, never at peace, forever bent on slandering men, bellowing like a maddened elephant—him one should forsake as one would a most savage dog.

sanskrit: adhīrajuṣṭe pathi vartamānaṃ; damād apetaṃ vinayāc ca pāpam arivrataṃ nityam abhūtikāmaṃ; dhig astu taṃ pāpamatiṃ manuṣyam
english: Walking the path frequented by the irresolute, fallen away from self-control and from good breeding, evil, ever bent on hostility and on others' ruin—shame upon that man of wicked mind!

sanskrit: pratyucyamānas tu hi bhūya ebhir; niśāmya mā bhūs tvam athārtarūpaḥ uccasya nīcena hi saṃprayogaṃ; vigarhayanti sthirabuddhayo ye
english: Even when answered back by these men again and again, hearken and do not grow distressed; for the steadfast of mind condemn any contest between the high and the low.

sanskrit: kruddho daśārdhena hi tāḍayed vā; sa pāṃsubhir vāpakiret tuṣair vā vivṛtya dantāṃś ca vibhīṣayed vā; siddhaṃ hi mūrkhe kupite nṛśaṃse
english: In his rage he might strike with the flat of his hand, or pelt one with dust or with chaff, or bare his teeth to terrify—for all this is to be expected of a fool grown angry and cruel.

sanskrit: vigarhaṇāṃ paramadurātmanā kṛtāṃ; saheta yaḥ saṃsadi durjanān naraḥ paṭhed idaṃ cāpi nidarśanaṃ sadā; na vāṅmayaṃ sa labhati kiṃ cid apriyam
english: The man who in the assembly bears with the reproach heaped on by the basest of wretches, and who ever recites this instruction concerning the wicked, suffers nothing unpleasant that words can bring.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pitāmaha mahāprājña saṃśayo me mahān ayam sa cchettavyas tvayā rājan bhavān kulakaro hi naḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Grandfather, greatly wise, this is a great doubt of mine; it must be resolved by you, O king, for you are the founder of our line.

sanskrit: puruṣāṇām ayaṃ tāta durvṛttānāṃ durātmanām kathito vākyasaṃcāras tato vijñāpayāmi te
english: O father, the traffic of words of men of evil conduct and evil mind has been told; and so I ask of you further.

sanskrit: yad dhitaṃ rājyatantrasya kulasya ca sukhodayam āyatyāṃ ca tadātve ca kṣemavṛddhikaraṃ ca yat
english: What is beneficial for the machinery of the kingdom and brings happiness to the family, and what conduces to security and increase both in the future and in the present—

sanskrit: putrapautrābhirāmaṃ ca rāṣṭravṛddhikaraṃ ca yat annapāne śarīre ca hitaṃ yat tad bravīhi me
english: and what delights sons and grandsons and furthers the increase of the realm, and what is wholesome in food and drink and for the body—tell that to me.

sanskrit: abhiṣikto hi yo rājā rājyastho mitrasaṃvṛtaḥ asuhṛt samupeto vā sa kathaṃ rañjayet prajāḥ
english: A king who has been consecrated, established in his kingdom and surrounded by friends—or else beset by those who are no friends—how should he win the love of his subjects?

sanskrit: yo hy asatpragraharatiḥ sneharāgabalātkṛtaḥ indriyāṇām anīśatvād asajjanabubhūṣakaḥ
english: For one who delights in favouring the wicked, overborne by affection and passion, who through want of mastery over his senses craves the company of base men—
